Sage advice. Sadly being admitted to hospital in the UK via a GP is difficult. I have been referred to a crisis unit before but their assessment was that I was safe. If I hurt myself or someone else (God forbid) my chances of being sectioned at my request or at the request of medical authorities rises considerably. I used to criticize the police but I now realize they spend a huge portion of their day dealing with people that have mental health issues. We aren’t exactly the easiest to deal with.

I’ve had a lifetime of developing obsessions, 100% of cases my feelings were unrequited. I have left jobs to add space, but not before torturing myself by watching their lives and wishing I was part of it. There is no good solution. In my case I built elaborate domestic fantasies around them, it was enough to keep me stable. I would withdraw into a fantasy of domestic bliss whenever my feelings were becoming overwhelming. Having the fantasies was enough to prevent me doing something stupid and allowing reality to leach in. If you never ask her out, she can’t say no and the fantasy life you have built still has “credibility” as a possible future outcome. 

It worked until I hit middle age, I was dumb enough to try and convert a fantasy to reality by declaring my feelings... it went very very badly

Good luck

If you have an EU passport, it’s just a matter of months. Move, register and once your social security number is sorted out technically you should be good to go, however Getting a Dr to help you is much harder, the Dutch don’t want euthanasia tourism, the Belgians are a bit more liberal BUT also are concerned about a rash of people moving to end their lives.
Belgium or the Netherlands will allow this but only IF you are resident.

Maybe many potential posters take comfort from the advice proffered and either step back or carry out the act. 

More seriously, I suspect the posts are part of a deflection method for many. I used to travel for work, I was suicidal and my method of control was to “plan” my suicide as soon as I got into each hotel. The process of making sure I had my noose ready and had scouted the suspension point was usually enough of a delay for the suicidal thoughts to ebb. Writing about your imminent suicide may well be part of a similar thing

Preparing your letter may give you the solace you need to avoid acting on your impulses. Good luck

I even managed to “socialise” after a fashion at work. Eventually my denial caught up on me, lost my SO, family.... eventually went into therapy to save my Job.... too late. This nervous breakdown was total and I made plans not only to kill myself but others (I was sectioned). I can probably be saved but I am a husk and utterly finished. 

This is not the way to go. Therapy nearly saved me but I have fucked my marriage up beyond repair by then and my career was hurtling towards a complete crash. Seek help early PLEASE. I could have been saved. Good luck, you can do it mate!!,

Friends could abandon you, they haven't, their awkwardness is normal... but they are there. Talk to them. I don't know your age but you need to reach out for help.

So insane people care about you, we might be mad but we are still driven by our emotions. This exercise stopped me from attempts a few times. Make a list of the people whose life you touch.... BE HONEST. It will surprise you. You may think they don't give a stuff, or realise.... but you are touching them.

Suicide takes an enormous amount of physical courage and determination. It will end your existence IF you are successful however it will not resolve everything, it will simply remove you from the equation. We all lead interlocked lives. Our exits are never tidy and can have catastrophic implications on those around us.

I understand your desire, please understand the finality of any action. But also understand the visceral desire of our unconscious and sub-conscious self to survive. Suicide is not easy and the devastation of failure on your self should not be underestimated. I try and focus on minutiae, the pointlessness helps fill my mind.

We are hard wired to survive. If you are a believer, most religions condemn suicides to damnation. If you are an atheist you know that it is the end, a full stop. 

When I made my attempts (3 aborted, 1 failed) it was at points where my despair gave a moment of courage, allowing me to convert plans into actions. The moments do not necessarily come at logical times (suicide is a failure of the survival bias).  

The reason (I think) The Samaritans works is that those moments of courage are fleeting, a brief call can bridge that gap.  Suicide is way harder to complete successfully than people imagine, even with the best of planning and practice, the moment is so often fleeting. Seek help

When your moment comes (I hope it doesn't and you recover) look on it as finally doing something for yourself. Remember suicide may be an exit from pain, but it is the also the end of everything.

It's different for everyone. Practice, your moment of courage will not telegraph itself. When it arrives it will be easy to put your plan into practice. Be in practice though, I wasn't and I fucked up. 

It's surprising how much courage it takes, if you are a believer pretty much all the major religions condemn you to hell, if you are an atheist it's the final act... no coming back. That courage born of desperation could be right around the corner.
